40f6d2e17f56819ea683f45a30072086.body:
> Build the Content extension on an existing OSM foundation. Reuse the owner's Notion home and general business context. Create only missing content-specific structure; keep originals, identities and useful integrations.

## Before you create anything

Read the owner's exact AI operating model home (or existing Data & Context entry) and selected operating policy. Find their existing Knowledge, Memory and personal Skills routes. Locate the current goals, audience, offers, voice and working preferences. These remain business context in Knowledge; this extension does not create a second strategy or Goals database.

Inspect the existing content workflow, database schema, integrations and media locations. A ready OSM setup does not imply a Content database exists. A similar title does not identify the canonical database. Record whether you will reuse, adapt or create, and resolve only missing choices that affect this work.

An explicit request to set up this extension normally covers the missing collection and ordinary properties inside the owner's authorized home; reuse that authority. Inspect both schema dependencies and row-level triggers before writing: a new row, Type/Status choice or checkbox can publish to a website, send mail or trigger another system. Do not use an integrated destination for a sample until the chosen draft state is confirmed non-publishing. Unknown destinations, consequential changes to an integration or new external access need a concrete resolution; they are not permission to create another account or content mirror.

## One collection, three record types

| Type | What it owns | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source | A reference, raw observation, transcript or inspiration and our annotation | A saved article or recording reference |
| Content | An idea growing into a production, with one stable identity | An explanation based on real work |
| Edition | An independently edited version for a format or destination | A LinkedIn post or newsletter derived from that production |

An idea can become a production on the same Content record. Create an Edition when it has its own editable text, packaging, review or delivery. One newsletter may use several sources or productions. A Source keeps its own state when something derived from it is published.

## Baseline properties

These are meanings and starter names, not a migration command. Map suitable existing properties before adding columns. Record the actual property names, types and canonical database/data-source IDs in the owner's configuration.

| Property | Starter Notion type | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | Title | Human-readable subject |
| Key | Rich text | Stable record identity; retain an existing key, otherwise create a durable origin-based or generated key |
| Type | Select: Source, Content, Edition | Record responsibility |
| Status | Select | State within that responsibility, using the transitions below |
| Summary | Rich text | Short current explanation, searchable without loading the whole body |
| Source URL | URL | External original when one exists; keep other origins in the body |
| Source date | Date | Actual origin/event date, if known; never the import date by default |
| Sources | Self-relation, multiple | Links to the actual Source records used |
| Derived from | Self-relation, multiple | Links an Edition to its Content parent(s), or a deliberate adaptation to its predecessor |

For a new collection, create the ordinary columns first, read its actual data-source ID, then add self-relations using that ID and verify both ends. Do not put a database block ID where a data-source ID is required. Prefer one-way relations unless a useful reciprocal view justifies paired properties. Never retarget a populated relation without a checked migration.

Notion does not enforce Key uniqueness. Record the owner's key convention in configuration; query the key/origin and semantic overlap before creating. For a URL source use the verified canonical origin without stripping meaningful query parameters. For another new record choose a durable generated key before the first create, retain that key through the attempt and reuse it on retry. A source URL does not identify an independently edited edition. Serialize a shared writer where needed. After an uncertain create, inspect that key and actual service result before any retry; never mint a new key just because the response was lost.

## Add metadata where the workflow uses it

| Property | Suggested type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medium | Select | Text, video, audio or mixed; independent of platform |
| Format | Rich text or existing Select | How-to, reflection, showcase, interview or another useful form |
| Channels | Multi-select | Only the owner's selected destinations; do not activate every platform |
| Revised | Date, optional | A substantive record, method or editorial-annotation change; not blanket reverification |
| Review due | Date, optional | A justified reconsideration point; keep the reason beside the affected claim |
| Publish date | Date | Verified time for the primary delivery, or omitted when ambiguous; the per-destination section remains authoritative |
| Public URL | URL | Actual primary output when available; multiple deliveries retain their own URLs in the delivery section |
| Last updated by | Native last-edited-by, or an existing explicit client field | Preserve the distinction between the API actor and a known editing client; do not invent an author |
| Created / Last edited | Native system fields, if useful | Technical record times, never evidence freshness |

Reuse source/import/processing fields already present. Do not overwrite them with Revised, backfill unknown dates with today, or add a universal recency score. Reads, imports, formatting and unchanged runs do not bump Revised. Review due is a review signal, not expiry or falsehood. On a Source, Revised dates our annotation; the external original retains its own date. Personal skill source/version remains separate from its record revision.

## Practical starter states and views

Use one Select with only the values needed by the chosen workflow; map existing values deliberately. These type-specific transitions are a starter:

| Type | Normal progression | What allows the transition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source | Inbox → Reviewed, or Archived | The source/coverage was actually inspected; Reviewed does not mean every external claim was verified. A derivative's publication never publishes the Source. |
| Content | Inbox → Selected → Preparing → Material ready → Producing → Ready → Scheduled / Published only for direct delivery | The owner or configured selection policy selects it. Material ready requires actual accessible text/media and a known revision. Ready requires the configured review of the finished original. |
| Edition | Preparing / Producing → Ready → Scheduled / Published | Ready requires the configured review, including a human where selected. Scheduled needs the service's real job ID; Published needs verified delivery evidence. |

Paused, Needs review and Archived are optional across types. Agents may perform the configured review when the owner's policy permits it; self-review does not replace a required human/independent gate. Never infer publication authority from Ready. A directly published original can retain its delivery section on the Content record when that is the existing configured workflow; no duplicate editable body is required.

For each selected destination retain its delivery state, actual revision, account, date/URL or send/job ID in a delivery section. One edition may have several deliveries. Failed and Outcome unknown describe real delivery results; if some destinations succeeded, retain Partially published until the others are reconciled. Do not let one public URL erase a failed email. Add those Select values only when used; the delivery section is authoritative for the individual results.

Start with a few views of the same records: Inbox; Ideas (Type Content); In production; Editions (Type Edition); Sources/library (Type Source); Follow-up (Needs review, failed/unknown delivery or Review due, where selected). A due view does not replace useful new evidence or route drift. Do not add another measurements database or dashboard until its scale warrants one.

## Keep bodies useful

Use only the sections a record needs:

- Source: original location/attribution, why saved, useful excerpt or supported annotation, source date/coverage and uncertainty. For creative references, record the specific technique and relevant time range; follow the [reference-library workflow](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-Content/blob/v0.11.0/docs/reference-library.md) when it informs reusable guidance.
- Content: angle, chosen goal and its Knowledge reference/revision, audience, evidence, brief/script, actual material links, and next useful action. A goal revision is its owning record link plus Revised/version, or an explicit selected statement/date when no semantic revision exists; preserve that selection rather than inventing a date.
- Edition: parent/source links, editable body or media-project reference, destination, reviewed version, delivery evidence and dated feedback.

A brief is not footage. A Source summary is not the full transcript. Separate original words, our annotation and a proposed angle. Preserve human writing and useful prior reasons while revising the affected current section instead of appending a contradictory history.

## Video and other large files

Notion is the editorial index and context home, not mandatory storage for large footage or project files. Keep media in an owner-selected local or cloud location and the actual editor project in its chosen workspace. Record the original's location, meaningful revision, relevant assets and access route on its production; keep real clip time ranges when excerpts exist.

Record who owns storage/backup and what the agent can actually access. A link is not a backup. A local path is scoped to its host, not a universal data location. Do not upload private footage to a cloud service to bypass a missing route. Existing editors, external editorial originals and analog material can stay; map one editable original and its handoff rather than making a competing copy.

## Register and verify

1. Save the real Content route, field map, chosen views and configuration reference in the owner's existing definition/context. Preserve general goals and policy ownership.
2. Adapt only the useful skill templates into the owner's personal Skills through the available skill-management method. Check existing methods and collisions first; keep their selected versions/references and human originals.
3. Exercise one bounded authorized example in a verified non-publishing state: capture a source/idea, prepare the needed material, and follow its actual next handoff. Do not publish just to prove setup. A repeat capture/setup must reuse identities. For a one-off capture without saved configuration, inspect the actual schema, key convention and integration-safe draft state, reuse standing write authority and resolve only material gaps. Full setup or a new configuration record is not a prerequisite for that isolated safe task.
4. Report separately what is mapped, created, adapted, enabled/discoverable, actually exercised and still missing. A saved skill page is not proof of native discovery or installation.

Existing OSM upkeep can maintain this selected collection and definition under its normal policy. Setup does not create a second daily writer, a production schedule, subscriber sync or outbound publication.

> Make this the owner's workflow. Keep the shared method and its templates as references; save the actual choices in private Knowledge and adapted methods in the owner's Skills. Content vision remains a useful human reference, not a place to append production logs. ## Reuse the business foundation Read the existing goals/vision, audience, offers, positioning, voice, channels and working preferences. Link their actual owning records and revisions. Resolve a missing business decision there rather than creating a competing Content strategy. A creator can pursue suitable enquiries, sales, education, a community role, audience growth or another goal; do not silently optimize every business for followers. Select the goal per edition, not only per production. A single idea can build an audience on one channel and support customer dialogue on another. Record the reader, language, useful ending and relevant evidence for each. Reach, profile interest, video discovery and customer enquiries are different signals; none is a universal success measure. Monetization ideas remain provisional until the owner chooses them. Concrete observations stay with the Content record or edition, with date/window and uncertainty. For an ordinary post, use the [short-post workflow](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-Content/blob/v0.11.0/docs/post-workflow.md). Do not restart Setup. A link, brand mention, question or sales invitation is optional and follows the purpose of that edition. ## Make only the choices that change the work | Area | Record the actual choice | | --- | --- | | Starting material | Written work, recordings, spoken notes, existing content, analog notes or a combination | | Creative process | What the human wants to do; what AI may help with; outline versus full script; human editor or existing workflow | | Formats | A small useful set such as reflection/article, guide, how-to, showcase or direct short note | | Channels | Audience, language, useful format, contribution to the goal and sustainable effort for each active destination | | Editorial original | Where each kind of text/production is actually edited; Notion can index an existing external original | | Media/projects | Owner-selected storage, access, revision and backup responsibility; chosen editor and qualification status | | Delivery | Actual account/destination, draft/review path, applicable standing or task authority and where outcomes are recorded | | Learning | Relevant signals, observation window, sustainable effort and the next review/experiment | Notion for editorial text and Kit for newsletter delivery are a starter recipe; suitable existing tools can stay. HyperFrames is a candidate requiring a real import/edit/save-reopen/export qualification before use is claimed. None of these choices installs a tool or connects an account. A newsletter may be an original or a synthesis of several productions. Video, email, an article and a social post can each be long or short. Long-to-short reuse is useful when each edition has a self-contained point; do not force every idea into a long production or every production onto every channel. ## Keep creative references useful Use the [reference-library workflow](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-Content/blob/v0.11.0/docs/reference-library.md) when a creator example
should inform the owner's style. Keep the original and observations on its Source,
accepted choices in configuration, and reusable techniques in the existing style
or treatment guide. Update a personal skill only when its working steps change.
Each production selects the references it needs; a saved source is not automatic
adoption. Channel languages are owner choices, not shared defaults. ## Decide participation per responsibility | Responsibility | Useful configuration | | --- | --- | | Setup | Existing routes, reusable schema, missing structure and acceptance example | | Intake | Capture sources and useful angles; decide whether scouting is wanted | | Prepare | Writing/recording support, required evidence and material handoff | | Produce / Distribute | Selected editor, editions, review and actual delivery policy | | Learn | Goal-relevant observations and deliberate improvement | Each can be manual, assisted or selectively automated. A responsibility is not a mandatory separate skill or agent. Keep a good analog workflow. Missing input blocks only the dependent operation; an idea can still be captured while media editing is unavailable. For an automation, specify the real trigger/cadence and timezone, selected sources/account, bounded work, output, permitted actions, missing-input behavior, retry/reconciliation and native job identity. Create it only under applicable authority. Use the same adopted method as a manual invocation; no second implementation or background publisher hidden in a skill. ## Adopt personal skills The five public templates are starting material. Read and adapt the useful ones through the owner's available Manage Skills method. Do not require an unreleased OSM name: discover the actually installed capability or follow the selected home's supported personal-Skills procedure. Before writing, query the owner's Skills for semantic overlap and preserve useful existing instructions, supporting files and provenance. Choose discriminating names/descriptions, actual input/output locations and a reference to the accepted owner configuration. Shared methods stay outside that configuration. A bundle copied locally is not a native install or automatic enablement. The setup template uses the schema/setup contract. Other templates need only relevant goals, configuration and selected material. They do not re-interview the owner or recreate the database at every request. If the configuration is missing, resolve the actual gap rather than guess accounts, destinations or permission. ## A compact owner configuration Store the concrete choices in one short private Knowledge record using the owner's normal schema. Its body can contain this simple record, completed from evidence; these are descriptive fields, not an executable deployment format: ```yaml content_workflow: context_home: null content_collection: null field_map: {} key_convention: null integration_triggers_and_safe_states: [] goals_and_revisions: [] audience_and_voice_refs: [] editorial_originals: [] media_and_backup_routes: [] selected_channels: [] formats_and_preferences: [] stage_ownership_and_modes: {} tool_routes_and_qualification: {} delivery_policy: null observation_and_review: null adopted_personal_skills: [] actual_automation_ids: [] ``` Null/empty means unresolved or not selected, not a working default. Do not activate missing tools, delivery or schedules to fill this record. Capture the concrete blocker and continue independent useful work. Update configuration only when a supported choice changes; routine production belongs in Content. Each media route names its location, host where relevant, actual access and backup owner/status. Each adopted skill records its real personal-Skills location/ID, source template/version/hash, local adaptations and observed discovery/invocation state. Capture actual evidence; do not label a fetched page as enabled discovery. If neither skill management nor the home's supported Skills operation is available, report the exact gap and retain the proposed adaptation without creating an improvised second store. ## Ready to use Check one realistic task with the chosen methods and actual routes. Can a new agent find the owner's Content collection, avoid duplicates, preserve voice/originals, follow a material handoff and report actual results? Can it distinguish prepared, reviewed and published without this setup conversation? Start with one production and a few relevant editions. Revise the workflow from real use before adding more channels, tools or automation.

40d6d2e17f5681219a81e13317a19339.body:
Turn real work, ideas and references into content worth sharing. Keep your own voice, choose a purpose for each edition and learn from the response.

Content is a separate method kit for OSM. It uses the business foundation in your AI operating model home and can work with your existing tools and personal skills.

## Make one useful piece

1. Save the idea or reference and what interests you.
2. Choose the reader, purpose and your own contribution.
3. Write, record or edit the editions that help.
4. Review and deliver under your chosen publication authority.
5. Keep the result and one useful lesson.

For a single post, follow the [short-post workflow](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-Content/blob/3f50282dc06e21e8d0a5e34f74d6bbab2557febf/docs/post-workflow.md). A short idea can stand alone. Different channels can have different goals; a post may end with its point. A brand mention, link or invitation belongs where it helps the reader.

## Set it up once

<page url="https://app.notion.com/p/40f6d2e17f56819ea683f45a30072086">
Content setup & database
</page>

<page url="https://app.notion.com/p/40f6d2e17f5681d68525d83503a457d5">
Personal configuration
</page>

Reuse a suitable Content collection. Source keeps references and attribution; Content keeps an idea or production; Edition keeps an independently edited version and its actual delivery. Your private configuration selects goals, audiences, voice, channels, tools and personal skills. Keep media in its selected storage with an access and backup route. Reuse the existing direction/goals, audience and perspective, and voice/style records. Choose a useful role for each active channel, including newsletter/email as its own channel; the Personal configuration page gives examples without requiring every platform.

## Give this to your agent

```txt
Use OSM Content to help with my selected idea or workflow.
My AI operating model home is: [my own context-home link].

Read its selected policy and relevant content configuration. Reuse existing records and personal methods. Choose the purpose and reader for each edition, preserve my voice and the source attribution, then prepare the useful draft or material. Keep delivery within the authority I have actually given. Report the next useful action.
```

For initial setup, read the setup and configuration pages above. For ordinary writing, inspect only what the piece needs.

## Learn from references

Save the example with at least one concrete line per link about what you liked, plus a timestamp when relevant. Describe the specific technique and inspect what actually happens. Strengthen your own angle and add your own contribution. When a choice becomes reusable, update the relevant style guide or personal method and use it in the next production. Keep attribution and rejected examples clear.

[Reference workflow](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-Content/blob/3f50282dc06e21e8d0a5e34f74d6bbab2557febf/docs/reference-library.md)

## Adapt the methods you need

Setup, Intake, Prepare, Produce / Distribute and Learn are responsibilities. Existing personal skills can cover several; five new agents or skills are not required.

- <mention url="https://app.notion.com/p/40d6d2e17f5681578925cdc0774c6db5">content-setup</mention>
- <mention url="https://app.notion.com/p/40d6d2e17f5681c99020d85e3bc1ff4b">content-intake</mention>
- <mention url="https://app.notion.com/p/40d6d2e17f568141a2c9efa2d04c9268">content-prepare</mention>
- <mention url="https://app.notion.com/p/40d6d2e17f568122aa82f1dcf83500a7">content-produce</mention>
- <mention url="https://app.notion.com/p/40d6d2e17f5681c784c4d545814fd7a5">content-learn</mention>

Knowledge owns business context; Content owns sources, productions, editions and feedback. Adapted personal skills and actual preferences remain in the owner's private home. A saved skill is not proof of native installation or use. Choose and qualify tools for the actual task.

## Content foundation

## Source and versions

[OSM Content v0.12.1](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-Content/releases/tag/v0.12.1) is the shared method release. The retained v0.10.0 Draft templates are unchanged frozen packets from edition 2026-11-05.1; their files and history remain in the catalogue. This kit is outside the OSM plugin and starts no publishing schedule.

The repository owns shared changes; this guide is its readable companion. Accepted main changes and method releases can update it through the configured public-only documentation workflow. A conflicting manual edit is held for review. This synchronizes the shared guide, not personal drafts or social posts. [Documentation upkeep](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-Content/blob/3f50282dc06e21e8d0a5e34f74d6bbab2557febf/docs/maintenance.md) records the page mapping and checks. Private writing, media and configuration stay private.

Before writing, verify row-level integration triggers and a non-publishing draft state as well as property types. Choose or reuse a stable key before create, retain it through uncertainty and query it before retry; do not generate another key on a lost response. A one-off safe capture can use inspected mappings without forcing a saved configuration or full setup. Capture can be a conversation: accept a rough braindump and useful follow-up corrections without forcing a form. Before creating a record, reconcile stable source ID/URL and semantic overlap, including parked material. Preserve the original words and attribution; distinguish editorial notes and inferred angles. Unknown source dates and unread links remain explicit. A correction updates the existing idea instead of creating another copy. Store why the owner saved it, the real source/location, relevant context and one concrete next action when needed. Treat third-party inspiration, the owner's raw ideas and explicitly approved voice examples differently; do not infer voice approval from an AI draft or public performance. Propose a few useful perspectives tied to the actual audience and selected goal. Include what the owner can substantiate or add. A source's popularity is not evidence that its claims apply to this business. Keep personal observations when they serve a real editorial purpose; every capture does not need a direct sales pitch. When an idea is selected for production, link one primary goal and, when useful, a secondary goal with the relevant revisions. Capture alone does not require choosing every field. Suggest written, recorded, combined, or direct short form where it helps. Long form is not a mandatory prerequisite. Do not mark a proposed idea Selected unless the owner or the configured decision policy selected it. Saving can be the whole task. Return the real record/readback link and a concise angle/next step; continue to Prepare only when that work is requested or already covered by the selected workflow. For scheduled scouting, use only the configured sources, criteria and bounded discovery window. New accounts or broad feed access are not implied. No worthwhile idea is a valid result. Do not turn the scout into an automatic production or publishing job. ## Adaptation and setup Read Personal configuration when adapting this template. Method v0.11.0 does not change this template's version or install a personal skill. ## Instructions Before creating a record or changing Status/flags, apply the configured key convention and integration triggers/safe states; inspect them first if unrecorded. Choose an edition key before create and query that retained key before retrying an uncertain outcome. Template edition 2026-11-05.1. Use the owner’s actual Content configuration and routes. Read Personal configuration when tailoring this into a personal skill; normal use loads only the selected configuration and relevant material. This template is not an installed or enabled method. Accept actual text, audio or footage with its original location/revision, chosen primary goal/revision, any secondary goal, audience, relevant voice/taste and delivery scope. Material may come from Prepare or an existing human workflow. Do not require the owner to recreate it through our earlier stages. Finish the original in the chosen tool. Notion is the reference editorial home; a video project owns its actual timeline/media edits. HyperFrames is one candidate. Use it only after practical qualification in this environment and availability of an actually reviewed operating skill; neither is established by this template. Preserve the chosen creative defaults. Keep a suitable existing editor or human editor when selected. Create only editions that have a useful purpose for their destination. A newsletter may be an original or a synthesis; a short text need not begin as a video. Adapt context, hook, length, image and next step to the actual channel/account constraints. Never claim a video extract exists without the real footage/time range. Keep an independently edited edition linked to its original/sources. Preserve one canonical body for shared text and separate actual deliveries. A library entry, Resources lesson, web article and email can reuse material without becoming competing editable originals. Review the actual final version for meaning, factual support, taste/voice, packaging and audience fit. Inspect exported video by seeing and hearing it, including audio sync, readable text, captions and ending. A screenshot or valid container is not video acceptance. The editing handoff is a reviewed edition ready for its destination. This does not mean it has been sent or published. ## Distribution Read the release contract below (also in the packet) when sending, scheduling or publishing. Prepare Kit subject/preview/body and relevant public companions when selected. Send, schedule or publish only under the applicable exact or standing destination/version authority. A standing automated policy need not ask again for every routine release; a draft request supplies no send authority. Record the actual state and verified result per destination, including unknown or partial outcomes as defined by the selected configuration and setup contract. Reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying to prevent duplicate sends/posts. A failed email does not erase a successful web delivery. Return real output links/IDs and remaining input; do not invent publication or marketing results. ## Adaptation and setup Read Personal configuration when adapting this template. The portable packet includes references/adaptation.md. Actual private routes, configuration and creative choices belong to the adopting owner; no private data is needed in this public template. ## Release contract Use the actual destination and the reviewed edition/revision. A prepared or reviewed edition is not a delivery. 1. Resolve the applicable exact or standing authority: destination/account, version or selection policy, timing and permitted action. Reuse existing permission; a draft request alone supplies no send authority. 2. Verify the final edition and packaging in the selected tool. Keep canonical material and independent channel editions linked. 3. Deliver only the selected action. Editing, review and outward delivery remain distinct even when one skill or an authorized automation carries them through. 4. Record actual per-destination state and output identity: ready, scheduled, published/sent, failed or outcome unknown. One successful destination is not rolled back by another's failure; keep Partially published plus exact per-destination evidence until unresolved deliveries are reconciled. 5. For an unknown outcome, inspect the service's actual send/post/job identity before retrying. Never create a second send merely because a response timed out. 6. Report real output links/IDs and unresolved input. Do not infer enquiries, attribution or sales from a successful publication. Daily upkeep may reconcile supported delivery facts and owner-stated decisions under its selected policy. Editorial learning chooses experiments and proposes strategic/taste changes; it does not silently redefine goals. An explicit owner correction may be curated at its actual Knowledge owner.

A supported reusable conclusion can update its owning configuration in Knowledge under the actual authority; generic skill changes are deliberate revisions. Preserve human taste and chosen goals rather than silently redefining them around the latest popular post. This step can be manual, assisted or a configured recurring review.
